edbDesc: An alloy that 'remembers' its original, cold-forged shape: returning the pre-deformed shape by heating. This material is a lightweight, solid-state alternative to conventional actuators such as hydraulic, pneumatic, and motor-based systems.
title: Shape-memory alloy
description: A bent wire of nickel-titanium snaps back to its original shape when warmed, as if it remembered it. Buehler's team at the US Naval Ordnance Laboratory found it in their alloy Nitinol, and it now opens heart stents inside arteries and shuts off scalding shower water on its own.
effect: a bent metal returns to its remembered shape when heated
strength: A nitinol wire as thin as a pencil lead can lift a few kilograms as it shrinks back by about 4 percent when warmed.
pickWhy: Clear actuator effect with many uses; dated to Nitinol (1962), though the effect was glimpsed in gold-cadmium in the 1930s-50s. Pseudoelasticity (another batch) is the same family and could merge here.
